speaker: Ms Valerie Lee
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Ministry has studied ways to encourage a shift towards more outcome-based work arrangements, rather than structured time-based models, where appropriate; and (b) what measures are in place to support employers and employees in adopting such practices while safeguarding productivity and employee well-being.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: However, such a model may not be suitable for jobs that would require shift work or a physical presence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Many professionals, managers and executives (PMEs) already work on the basis of delivering successful outcomes with limited tracking of work hours.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: As our workforce profile and the nature of jobs continues to evolve, we may expect more employers and employees to adopt such flexible work arrangements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: As part of implementation, employers and workers should mutually agree on the outcomes and how to track them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Government also supports employers in adopting technology and redesigning jobs through enterprise and workforce transformation initiatives so that work can be done more efficiently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This enables workers to deliver higher value in less time, improving productivity and enabling outcome-based approaches to work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Even as some work arrangements move towards outcome rather than time-based management, we recognise the need for employees to have healthy work-life boundaries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Such practices could include not requiring employees to respond to non-urgent work-related messages and emails until the following working day.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Has the Ministry studied the correlation between flexible results-oriented work models with productivity?

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: And second, this question honestly was inspired by one of my residents who work for the Ministry.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Has the Government, for public servants, demonstrated a work performance management system that weighs heavily on outcomes rather than time spent at work, meaning a Government-led work performance management system?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: They appreciate such arrangements because they will have flexibility in taking care of their children, they have flexibility in providing caregiving needs as required.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: In fact, this conversation should be between workers and employers as well – having a good conversation on what are the performance work outcomes required, and what are the tools and redesigning of the workplaces required to achieve productivity increases.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: In terms of performance, we leave it to the market and also the employers to determine what is the best performance and what is value for money.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: For the second one, within Ministries in terms of requiring work performance, I think, there is always a balance.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: Also, because within the Government, there is a myriad of roles.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: Some require presence and time, especially for security personnel, and some are mainly pure outcomes.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: And so, we work in very different ways and based on that tiering, we leave it to the supervisors to manage the staff and how they deliver those outcomes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If I may build very quickly on the second supplementary question by Member Valerie Lee.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I am wondering the extent to which the Government actually monitors and ensures that Government-affiliated institutions, such as our autonomous universities, also respect these kinds of flexible work arrangements.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I ask because of news reports that speak to how academics at the National University of Singapore, where outcomes are certainly the main way that we measure academic performance and are nevertheless forced to spend a significant amount of time in the office even though outcomes ultimately are the way that their performance is measured.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: In fact, flexible work arrangements are considered pretty nascent.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: I think the entire job market is also learning.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: Employers and employees are learning how to make those requests and employers are learning different ways in terms of flexi load – whether it is flexi place, flexi time as well – on how they deliver flexible work arrangements.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: On that note, in terms of the autonomous universities, it is an autonomous university.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: We leave it to the universities to decide how they determine outcomes and performance, and we encourage them to have deeper conversations with their employees and staff on their flexible work arrangements.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: And if they need any help, they can always approach Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices; if not, the Institute for Human Resource Professionals; if not, then NTUC.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: There are many toolkits and resources made available online and we are happy to help with that conversation.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Order of the Day.

speaker: Mr Speaker
